etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English tost, from the verb tosten (see below).

(person who is honored with a drink): First appears in print at the very end of the 17th century. The conventional assumption is that the use is metaphorical, “the name of a lady being supposed to flavour a drink like a spiced toast.” This is pure speculation, however, as the origin of the sense remains obscure.

(something that will be no more): Ad-libbed by actor Bill Murray in the 1984 film Ghostbusters (see quotation).

quote.text: Tea was a very special institution, revolving as it did around the ceremony and worship of Toast. In [public schools] where alcohol, tobacco and drugs were forbidden, it was essential that something should take their place as a powerful and public totem of virility and cool. Toast, for reasons lost in time, was the substance chosen.

definitions.definition: (countable) A proposed salutation (e.g. to say "cheers") while drinking alcohol.
(countable) A person, group, or notable object to which a salutation with alcohol is made; a person or group held in similar esteem.

quote.citation: 2014 May 28, John McWhorter, “Saint Maya”, in The New Republic‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: Josephine Baker did not become the toast of Paris by just shaking her booty for some theater gypsies as a party wound down.

definitions.definition: (uncountable, slang, chiefly US) Something that is irreparably damaged or used up, especially when destroyed by heat or fire; something which has been burnt to a crisp or incinerated.
(uncountable, slang, chiefly US) Something that will be no more; something subject to impending destruction, harm or injury.

quote.citation: 1984, Ghostbusters, spoken by Peter Venkman (Bill Murray):
quote.text: This chick is toast!The original line was: "I'm gonna turn this guy into toast."

definitions.definition: (countable, music, slang, Jamaica) A type of extemporaneous narrative poem or rap.
(countable, slang, obsolete) An old toast ("a lively fellow who drinks excessively").
(countable, computing, graphical user interface) A transient, informational unclickable pop-up overlay, less interactive than a snackbar.

quote.citation: 2012, Nick Lecrenski, Doug Holland, Allen Sanders, Professional Windows 8 Programming:
quote.text: With the new Windows Push Notification Service, you can remotely send notifications from a cloud-based web service. In Windows 8, the majority of the Toast messages are standard duration toasts.

definitions.definition: (countable, obsolete outside India) A piece of toast.

quote.citation: c. 1597 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Merry Wiues of Windsor”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene v], page 52, column 1:
quote.text: Go, fetch me a quart of Sacke, put a toſt in't.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tosten, from Old French toster (“to roast, grill”), from Latin tostus (“grilled, burnt”), from verb torreō (“to burn, grill”).

definitions.definition: To lightly cook by browning via direct exposure to a fire or other heat source.
To grill, lightly cook by browning specifically under a grill or in a toaster
To engage in a salutation and/or accompanying raising of glasses while drinking alcohol in honor of someone or something.
(music, slang, Jamaica) To perform extemporaneous narrative poem or rap.

quote.citation: 2014, Richard James Burgess, The History of Music Production, Oxford University Press, →ISBN, page 168:
quote.text: Toasting over a record does more than change the way that record is perceived by the audience: it creates a new piece of music with joint creative authorship, although the law does not support this characterization.
